_comment: Duck was standing on everything EXCEPT its tyres. Measured in game space through the loader: the rear wheels' tread bottoms out at y=0.277 and the front pair at y=0.282, but four other parts hang below that line and grounding rests the model on whichever reaches lowest — so the shipped bot floated 0.277ft up with all four wheels in the air. tools/repairs/duck-plow-tabs.json took the two worst prongs off the plow (part 6) but the same scan artefact is filed under three OTHER parts, and the plow's own lip still reached 0.159. This is one plane cut through every part that dips below the tyres: game-space y < 0.290 (0.013 clear of the rear tread, which leaves the cut edge just above the floor rather than through it once the triangle-centroid test rounds it). Wheels (parts 0,1,9,10) and the red beak (part 4, lowest vertex 0.286) are NOT in the list, so the rear tyres become the lowest geometry in the model and grounding lands them on the deck. Converted with rig-inspect --toglb: Duck's yaw is +PI/2, so game x maps to GLB z, game z to GLB -x, and the y plane 0.290 is GLB y -0.0260.

tripo_part_3 is the worst of them: an amorphous scan blob at the +x front (game x 0.255..1.340, z -1.089..-0.864) that melts from the bodywork all the way down to y=0.000 — the ONLY geometry in the whole model touching the floor, and therefore the thing the entire machine was balanced on. The real bot has nothing there; the reference shows clear air between the front wheel, the hinge block and the plow. Same plane, same region as the op above.

The white plow itself (modelWeapon's big panel). Its lip reached y=0.159, a tenth of a foot BELOW the tyres, so even with every stray removed the machine would still have sat on the plow with the wheels spinning in the air. Cut at the same plane; the open shell edge left along the bottom is closed again by tools/repairs/duck-plow-lip.json.
tripo_part_7 is the -x hinge/motor pod, the mirror of part 2. Same stray prong under it at game z -1.04..-0.84 reaching y=0.145. Same plane, same region.
